This is due to a new invoicing system we gradually started to adopt in mid-2022 called Dynamic Commission. Drivers' or Fleets' bonuses are now aggregated in their commission and the final sum is displayed only as one row: the commission row. For example;

Commission: 100€, Bonuses 25€, Booking Fee 15€, Refunds 10€

Driver will only see a single row in their commission invoice in the amount of 50€ (100-25-15-10).

More info about dynamic commission [here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/3663265890].



the calculation of monthly commission does this way that  we are taking less commission from the driver because we are subtracting from the total Fee (App orders) - all bonuses/compensations/ride discounts

To calculate ride discounts ( need to export all orders for the same period and calculate the difference between the client payed and the ride price)

For more information regarding dynamic commission please reach out Local OPS team, thanks

## The only exception that allows Bolt to terminate couriers without a 30 day’s notice is when a courier *repeatedly* breaches or fails to comply with any of the obligations set out in T&C. This means that a courier shall be given a chance to improve his behaviour for at least 2 times before we permanently block him/her claiming repetitive breach of rules.

Hey!

This is a good question and I think there is no good answer here, because these are the circumstances we must consider:

→ The aim of damage compensation is restoring the situation that we were in before the incident. This means, we should be using “market value” as the benchmark. 

→ The market value does not equal to our losses. Why? The prices for us (for bulk purchase) are not the same as the prices for a natural persons. In addition, we can deduct the VAT, so this will reduce the damage claim against the natural person (as a rule; this has to be checked with the tax team).

→ Under no circumstances should we making any profits from the damage claim processing. It is okay to cover reasonable costs (like: price evaluation, auctioning off, administrative fees). 

→ If we are facing a consumer, it would be good to have proof of purchase (or equivalent) to claim damages. Although, damage compensation can occur in the future, the basis for claim compensation should proven. 

→ In EE the supreme court has stated: _The matter_ (aka the destruction of the motor vehicle) _must be remedied on reasonable terms, i.e. the injured party_ (Bolt) _must choose the most favourable option wherever possible. If the injured party allows unnecessarily expensive repairs to be carried out, they will be in breach of the obligation to reduce the damage, which will lead to a corresponding reduction in their compensation. /.../ The amount of damages must be sufficient to enable the victim_ (Bolt) _to acquire an equivalent item at the time of compensation. In determining the amount of damages, the court must take into account the cost of acquiring an equivalent object as far as possible at the time of the judgment._

Considering the above said, in my opinion, the more-or-less correct approach could be:

# Determining the market value of the vehicle
# Determining the price of the same vehicle purchased off the line
# Determining the ratio of “market price” : “off the line vehicle”
# Applying the calculated ratio to the prices applicable for us.

I will try to demonstrate my train of thought:

* Volkswagen T-Roc Style 1.5 110kW, was in an accident and it was a write-off. We actoned it off and got *8700 EUR* (it was sold to Lithuania).
* The comparable market price is 26500 EUR (with VAT) or *22083 EUR* (0% VAT):

!Screenshot 2023-10-16 at 09.24.22.png|width=1035,height=673!



* The off-the-line price is 33040 EUR (20% VAT) or *27533* EUR (w/o VAT).

!Screenshot 2023-10-16 at 09.14.03.png|width=1051,height=200!



* So the current price to new price ratio is (22083/27533) or *0,8*
* Let’s say Moller gives us the same vehicle for *24 000 EUR* (w/o VAT)

So, in my mind, the calculation would be:

*(24 000 x 0,8) - 8700 = 10 500 EUR* (as base damage claim)

In addition, we would have costs related to cancelling the financing agreement, costs related to preparing the vehicle and selling it etc. In my opinion, these are justified costs and should be added to the claim (let’s say, they were all-in-all *500 EUR*).

So, the final damage claim would be *11 000 EUR* (in addition to any contractual penalties).

Through Upwork, companies are hiring independent service providers who normally can enter into agreements with service recipients without mandatory clauses. Regarding, Qatar, [here|https://worksuite.com/country-explorer/qatar/] I found a comparison between employment and independent contractors, the source says that _“There are minimal specific laws governing independent contractors. In general, laws covering employees also apply to independent contractors.“_ These minimal specific seem to be standard requirements as per any service agreement. 

* Further, even though it is the responsibility of the service provider to ensure they are properly registered in their tax residency country, it is also a basic duty of a service recipient to confirm that the individual is authorized to offer their services. Normally, a company should request +the candidates's proper registration (+[+sole proprietorship seems the most common form in Qatar+|https://www.deel.com/blog/register-a-sole-proprietorship-one-person-company-in-qatar]+) and make payments to the bank account associated with their registered business.+ 
* But it seems that in Qatar rules are not that strict. It is states that _“Qatari law_ *_does not legally distinguish between employees and independent contractors._* _Instead, the primary legal distinction is the citizenship status of the individual. Individuals who are citizens of Qatar or a GCC country only need a_ *_work permit_* _to engage in work, whether as an employee or independent contractor. However, it is likely they will have already established or be a partner in a company“.  “Hiring companies do not withhold any tax from independent contractors’ payments“._ 
* Per the above, it seems that in Qatar establishing of any business form is not necessary to provide services, instead having the right to work (citizenship) is sufficient. Thus, requesting a registration certificate is not mandatory. 
* When contracting with Upwork freelancers, we could signe both a service agreement and a separate agreement for intellectual property transfer and confidentiality (this could be covered by one agreement). In the service agreement it is advised to specify +that compliance with local laws, including obtaining necessary permits and paying taxes, is the full responsibility of the service provider. The service provider also commits to compensating the company in case any claims arise due to their violation of applicable laws.+
* However, since the primary service terms are already established through the Upwork platform (such as fees, service hours, and the scope of work), it does not seem mandatory to conclude a separate service agreement. Instead, it should be sufficient to sign the intellectual property transfer and confidentiality agreement while adding a clause regarding tax and registration compliance.

Let me know if I can help with this any further.

h3. User cannot reserve a vehicle/order a trip due to negative Bolt Balance

If the user has a negative Bolt Balance and travels to a country with a different currency, they won't be able to view their balance on the app anymore. Therefore, they won't be able to add funds to it or clear the debt. To resolve this issue, follow the steps outlined below:

*Step 1: Confirm charge details*

* Open User Balance > [Transaction history|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/user-balance/trxHistory] in Admin Panel
* Confirm there’s been a charge that caused a negative balance
* Look for a Booking that has: 💳 failed 🟢success
* Open the ride that caused the charge and check the date

*Step 2: Verify the cause*

* Open the Fraud > Calculations > [User page|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/fraud/userCalculationResults]
* Look for a decision REJECT TOP UP
** To ensure that the user cannot use the app because of debt, check for rows created on the same day or within one day.
* Is there a REJECT TOP UP decision?
** If yes, refund the trip that caused the debt to the user’s Bolt Balance
** If not, don’t refund the trip; advise the user they can use the app.

Hey!

In my opinion, this boils down to cost and what is the most reasonable way to cover the damages:
If we see that the repair is on par/more expensive than the selling, the vehicle should be sold. 

Tho, in that situation you described, it becomes a bit more complicated.

As a general remark, all the instances where insurance was involved, will be recorded and it becomes a public information. If we decide to opt for vehicle repair, this will eventually affect the sales price of the vehicle.

Based on that, we could justify the selling as the more economically sensible thing to do, as we would be charging them for the decreased value. 

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Grounds for reimbursement*
In the event of damage to the vehicle, compensation for damages covers in particular the reasonable costs of repairing the vehicle and the depreciation in value. Depreciation means a situation where the value of the vehicle, after it has been restored to a good standard, is less than its value before the damage.

Damage caused by depreciation is independent of whether the victim of the damage intended to sell the object or not.

Compensation for depreciation can be claimed by the owner of the vehicle. For example, in the case of damage to a leased vehicle, the lessor can claim depreciation. Whether and to what extent the lessor has to share the compensation with the lessee depends on their contract.

Theoretically, there can be two reasons for the depreciation of a vehicle.

Technical depreciation occurs when even a good quality repair cannot fully restore the vehicle to its previous technical condition.
In practice, this is not a problem, as any vehicle can be restored to its previous condition by means of appropriate repair technology.

+The economic depreciation reflects the difference between the market price of a vehicle that has been damaged and subsequently restored to a high standard and the market price of a similar undamaged vehicle. The fact that a vehicle has been involved in an accident is expected to influence the behaviour of potential buyers and the market price of a restored vehicle that has been involved in an accident is expected to be lower than that of a similar vehicle that has not been involved in an accident.+
{panel}

There might be merits for justifying the sales, but we should be able to show that the repairs would not restore the market value of the vehicle. Maybe as a part of the evaluation?

Driver will only see a single row in their commission invoice in the amount of 50€ (100-25-15-10).

The problem with schema changes is not related to the scheduled report itself. We can adjust the scheduled report with new schema changes with no issues. The issue with AWS AppFlow which we use to push the results into Salesforce.
Whenever we have a new field to map, AppFlow takes into consideration the schema of the first CSV file it finds in the bucket (so, the old files with the old schema), so we cannot map the new fields accordingly.
Unfortunately, this is a limitation on the AWS AppFlow side. I currently have access to delete/read on the other two buckets that we use, specifically because of this. Unless we remove the old files or create a new bucket whenever we have a schema change, we cannot adjust the field mapping on appflow.

Hey Octavian, the flow is called immutable for a reason. There is no tooling around managing this flow so any changes would require manual data manipulations. Which is error-prone. But no changes must be made to the raw immutable table.

*Estonia* - 3 years

The limitation period for a claim arising from a transaction is three years. 
The limitation period for damages is also three years from the time the parties should have become aware of the damage.
The limitation period for a claim provided for by law is ten years following the time when the claim fell due.

*Latvia* - 10 years

The general limitation period for contract and damage claims is 10 years in Latvia. If so provided by statutory act, the limitation periods in particular cases can be different - for example 2 years for employment claims.

*Lithuania* - 3 years

The limitation period for claims in tort, as well as for other damages claims (including claims for damages resulting from the inadequate quality of products), is three years. The general limitation period is 10 years.

Hi [~accountid:5b7bea6c358c9f2a008eab3e],

First of all, thank you for the idea – we used it to look at the global level data, too and built a [Reporting Behaviour Dashboard|https://bolt.cloud.looker.com/dashboards/16289?Report+Date=6+month+ago+for+6+month&Country=United+Kingdom&User+Persona=driver%2Crider&Period+to+Report=Up+to+1+Hour%2C1-2+Hours%2CUp+to+12+Hours%2CUp+to+24+Hours%2CMore+than+a+Day&Event+Category=-%25%21%25&Risk+Type+Looker+=&City+the+Event+Occurred+In=London]. Hopefully, it can be used to improve the product features and for making more educated choices in the future. We will be sharing it with relevant people soon.

In regards to your request, we had a look at it from multiple angles. There are *two measures* that could shed light on the reporting behavior:

* *Event date - Report date (Difference from Tool)* is the time period until an event emerged into a safety report, based on Global Event Assessment Tool data that is filled out manually by the agents, in hours. 
* *Order Created date - Ticket Created date (Real Difference)* is the time period from *order* creation till the appearance of a *support case*, in hours. 
We focus on the *latter* one as it’s more consistent.

----

We decided to look at the United Kingdom cases of a sexual nature for the past 12 complete months [separately|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/18SoK5uclUZex1Wa-PIhCvaZ_2B_qWIyWlWxWmRI2Ndc/edit#gid=0]. It gave us an opportunity to validate the Looker data and overcome some of the limitations of the dashboard: 

* use Beehive Ticket data, and
* manually fix obvious human errors.

Comparing *Tool-* and *Real-* hour durations, it seems that the deviation between average hours is within an hour. It can be likely related to the fact that the UK safety team is more selective on that matter but it also validates the *Order>Ticket* approach as it is of interest to us to know when the user had a first attempt of contacting us, no matter if they provided enough details for us to assess. 

On the spreadsheet, you can find a tab for *the* *UK* as a whole and *London* data, with:

* *GENERAL OVERVIEW OF VOLUMES*
Event categories and the corresponding number of cases, against 24h benchmark
* *OVERVIEW OF DURATIONS (IN HOURS)*
Against 24h benchmark, based on Admin (see first 2 tables) and Tool (see last 2 tables)
* *OVERVIEW OF 2ND DAY REPORTS*
Number of reports made on the second day since the order placement.

----

You can explore the Looker [dashboard|https://bolt.cloud.looker.com/dashboards/16289?Report+Date=6+month+ago+for+6+month&Country=United+Kingdom&User+Persona=driver%2Crider&Period+to+Report=Up+to+1+Hour%2C1-2+Hours%2CUp+to+12+Hours%2CUp+to+24+Hours%2CMore+than+a+Day&Event+Category=-%25%21%25&Risk+Type+Looker+=&City+the+Event+Occurred+In=London] yourself, but here are a few of my observations based on *ratios against a 24-hour benchmark*.

* Third party initiated events such as hijacking and robbery may likely affect the duration due to lack of access to accounts (global)
* Driver Contacted Rider After Journey –  this event by its nature happens *after* the journey, but the audio trip recording would not help much (London, 31% took more than 24h)
* Driver Touting and Driver Fraudulently Asked More Money (London, 25-27% took more than 24h)
* Accidents (London, 10-15% exceeding a day) – might be related to the nature of an event
* Drivers seem to report faster than riders (6% overall took more than a Day vs 11% of riders)
* Reports on driving style seem to be shared mostly *within* a day (globally, ~96%)

I’d suggest a further deep dive conducted into the reports that took more than 24 hours, to see if there are any specific patterns. *But generally, it seems that we can expect at least ~10% of reports that would be over the 24-hour benchmark.*

Please let me know if you have any questions.
Mariia

After long discussion with [~accountid:60acee2e317edd00718c5650] [~accountid:5eda5ad54ec4270ba37d2e87] and [~accountid:5e4fa9e0ab90210c8de1b9f7] , I might offer a simplified solution:

→ If we are talking about the value of the vehicle for us, it can be *market price* *x 0,85**. This is based on the price of vehicles sold from EE, LV, LT.

→ If we are talking about restoring the vehicle, we need the warranty for body works. This means, it has to made in the official agency. This means, the comparative price goes up.

The comparable market price is 26500 EUR (with VAT) or *22083* EUR (0% VAT):
The coefficient is *0,85*
(22083 x 0,85)-8700 =~*10100* EUR + other fees, ca 500 EUR

Coming back to your example:
Cost of the repair is *9500 EUR.*
The downtime for the vehicle is 2 months, no profit is generated, but we still have a capital cost. Let's say the cost is about *300 EUR* (2x [50+100] EUR) + other costs associated with the repair. 

We _could_ justify the first option by claiming the market value for the restored vehicle is lower, but this is not quite true as in accordance with the German value depreciation formula, it is assumed that rental cars cannot have their value depreciated.

+there is always an option to sell the vehicle, even if it’s not the economically feasible approach and not to claim the full amount aka taking the restoring value for reference.

*_Tambov constant_ - A universal quantity that must be added to, subtracted from, multiplied by or divided by the results of a measurement to obtain the required result.

This is due to a new invoicing system we gradually started to adopt in mid-2022 called Dynamic Commission. Drivers' or Fleets' bonuses are now aggregated in their commission and the final sum is displayed only as one row: commission row. For example;

Commission: 100€, Bonuses 25€, Booking Fee 15€, Refunds 10€

Driver will only see a single row in their commission invoice in the amount of 50€ (100-25-15-10).

technically [actual commission - bounses/compensations - rider discounts - booking fees = commission on the invoice]

More info about dynamic commission [here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/3663265890].

the report show the gross commission (the report shows the commission before all these discounts). on the invoice, the amount is all other things deducted from it (since commission netting is active).

# With the removal of the explicit node_code_owner tag, the values for node_code_owner are derived from the Prometheus query:
{noformat}sum  by (message,node_service_id, service_id )  (increase(nodejs:internal_request_client:responses_by_path{service_id="delivery-hex-cold-distance-matrix" , path="/internal/queryProviders", message="CITY_NOT_AVAILABLE(295802)" }[1m])){noformat}

The {{internal_request_client:responses_by_path}} metric is logged by the client (so {{node_code_owner}} is the _client_ owner), which is why only the client alerting channels have been notified.



To solve this we have defined a new Action [https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/backend-alerting/actions/edit/764|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/backend-alerting/actions/edit/764] so that our channel will also be notified when services we own are not responding correctly to our clients.

A note on the manual blocking responsibilities - currently all blocks aside from document blocks are with CS Tier-2 per the [UK escalation guidelines|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/7076414532114#additional-information-adding-and-removing-cs-blocks]. My concern is having multiple escalation points for different types of blocks. The current UK escalation guidelines are rather bulky based on the nature of the market, I would be mindful of adding varying guidelines for similar processes unless crucial.

On the other hand the escalation to OPS currently goes through Service Desk; based on the availability of the team, it takes a longer time to address the requests. [*RH processes & AI rules*|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1QbBd6FaTTkXtyaRSGruoKTyKE3HwkmhIzqGHkLjjWeA/edit#gid=255850940]

There are 13 issues (14 related processes), which will be solved with AI automation:

* :green_circle: *Refund, payment, verification, safety issues, and lost phone:* in these 7 situations AI will escalate the case to CS - no matching needs to be done here.
* :green_circle: *Account deletion:* AI will run all checks to make sure that the user is eligible for account deletion and only then will delete the account. Actions match our process.
* :green_circle: *Blocked account:* AI will explain in a message, why the account is blocked. Only if R keeps writing, the case will be escalated to CS (and then CS will be able to investigate further, escalate to the Tech team if necessary, etc.). Actions match our process.
* :yellow_circle: *Lost item:* less than 24hrs - message (R to contact the D), more than 24hrs - escalate to CS. It doesn’t fully match our process, as we don’t have the time distinction anymore, however, it won’t create friction because if R keeps writing to us, the case will be escalated to CS (e.g. if R can’t reach the D).
* :yellow_circle: *Unknown charge, double charge, pre-auth:* AI will try to close cases like pre-auth, or cases without actual charges with a message. Other cases, with actual charges, will get escalated to CS.
** I did a test and sent 2 messages to CS - 1 for the ride where I wasn’t overcharged, and 1 where I paid more. For the 1st one, I got a nice message from AI about pre-authorization, and the 2nd case got escalated to CS.

All in all, there is nothing to match, CS actions & AI rules can exist together without causing any friction to customers. :done:

	and date(a.created) >= date('2023-01-01')
	and date(a.created) <= date('2023-09-01')

	support_case_id 
	, case_language 
	, user_persona

	, case when case_language = country_code then true
		when case_language = 'en' then true

	and keyword_trigger <> 'n/a'
	and user_persona in ('driver', 'courier', 'fleet_owner', 'driver_lead', 'courier_lead', 'authority', 'courier_fleet_owner')

The reassignment test scenario proposal

# Create an organic event for a negative “commission” amount.
# Process the organic event - the commission invoice task should be created.
# Run the task processing cron - the commission should get reassigned to the next month.
# The *commission invoice task for the next month should be created.*
# (Potentially tweak the ignore_until, and) run the task processing cron. The records should be reassigned again.
# This time, add a positive commission record (or corresponding organic event & run the cron), so the invoice total becomes positive.
# Run the task processing cron again, this time the document should be created.

Steps 1 and 2 could be simplified, by creating a commission invoice task + commission record manually.
Having said that - in the next steps, Commission Invoice Tasks are created organically, so it makes sense to keep this level of abstraction also for the initial steps.

Similar flexibility is in the step 6, and I’d also prefer to use Organic Event. This way, additionally, we will test that the Commission Record Task created from Order Finished and Commission Record Task created from Commission Record Task itself, are the same task.

In principle, we would recommend not removing EU hosting as the EU-US Privacy Framework could be invalidated in the next 1-2 years. However, if the savings are big enough, it may justify the decision, provided that we have appropriate contractual mechanisms in place to satify privacy requirements for those transfers to the USA.

* In this case, I note that [*Okta*|https://www.dataprivacyframework.gov/s/participant-search] *has not Self-Certified to the EU-US Privacy Framework* - this means that we can’t rely on the Privacy Framework as a lawful mechanism to transfer data from the EU to the US as it wouldn’t apply to Okta. *Perhaps we can reach out to Okta and find out if they’re planning on doing so?*
* Okta is definitely processing personal data. 
* Either way, if we want to explore the possibility of +not+ storing data in the EEA, we will need a copy of Okta’s Data Processing Agreement to review, this would be to assess whether they have implemented appropriate SCCs, to understand where exactly data is going to go if not in the EEA, and to get a picture of their data retention and security practices.

This query shows the number of missing job runs in {{jobruncostpotentialfact}} per day:

{code:sql}%sql
with missing_runs as (
  select
    from_unixtime(time_detail.startTime / 1000) as start_time,
    to_date(from_unixtime(time_detail.startTime / 1000)) as start_date,
    jr.workspace_name as workspace,
    *
  from
    overwatch_spark.jobrun jr
    left join overwatch_spark.jobruncostpotentialfact jrc on jr.job_id = jrc.job_id
    and jr.job_run_id = jrc.job_run_id
  where
    jrc.job_run_id IS NULL
)
select
  start_date,
  workspace,
  count(*)
from
  missing_runs
group by
  start_date, workspace
order by
  start_date desc,
  workspace{code}

Let me provide you with some context first on the project - At the moment, we are *“silently”* collecting data, which means we are gathering information without taking any actions.

Our initial plan was to temporarily block accounts with suspicious names until users made the necessary changes and contacted our CS Team to get their accounts unblocked. However, due to the fact that our Terms and Conditions didn’t mention anything specific regarding to rider names - we were unable to proceed with this approach.

We worked closely with Stephanie Carvalho & other safety team members  with the intention of having the product team manage suspicious names and restrict their use during account creation/registration. Unfortunately, this initiative was also put on hold, as a legal consultant found that the occurrence of profanities among our rider base was relatively low. Please note that for the Paraguayan market, our criteria for "suspicious names" extends beyond sexual wording , as shown and explained on the assessment shared earlier (which includes criteria + # of suspicious names found up to last week) . Plus, the primary factor that has paused the process is the need for an update & localisation of the Terms and Conditions, which we have been informed that are not likely to be updated until next quarter.

Taking into account that this was a response to drivers request regarding safety, our objective is to *update & localise our T&C’s* *as soon as possible* to better align with the local market’s needs; given the fact that we have recently received lots of criticisms regarding safety issues on the platform (such as assaults, robberies, and acts of violence by passengers against drivers) as one of other safety measurements in which we are currently working, we see this update as esencial for the project's continuation and we would like to speed up the process if possible. 🙏  

Thanks!

_Dear [xxx]_

_Bolt understands the need to treat your investigation as confidential. Bolt also respects the request for data made by the police to help assist the police. We would like to assure you that Bolt will always seek to assist the police wherever we are legally able to do so._

_We are however concerned that your request, and inability to provide us with any context surrounding your request, makes it difficult for Bolt to execute our duties under Article 5 GDPR. Article 5 GDPR states that any data that is provided to a third party is adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary for the purposes for which the data is processed. For Bolt to be able to assess that the data requested falls under our duty of data minimisation, we ask that you provide high-level context to your investigation. Would would accept reference to the statue or law which you are looking to charge this suspect under. If this is not possible, we ask that you confirm this and consider reducing the scope of your request to data which is only strictly necessary for your investigation._

_Further, Bolt would like to advise you that the processing of this amount the amount of data you have taken would take a significant amount of time which would lead to further delays in providing the requested data. Therefore if you are able to provide any further data which would allow Bolt to reduce the amount of data shared, we would then be able to process your request more promptly._

_We wish to reiterate that any data shared by Bolt must be done so in accordance with GDPR and therefore all data shared must be necessary, relevant and proportionate to the claim which you are making. Aby spoločnosť Bolt mohla posúdiť, či sa na požadované údaje vzťahuje naša povinnosť minimalizovať údaje, žiadame vás, aby ste poskytli kontext na vysokej úrovni k vášmu prešetrovaniu. Ak to nie je možné, žiadame vás, aby ste to potvrdili a zvážili obmedzenie rozsahu vašej žiadosti na údaje, ktoré sú nevyhnutne potrebné len pre vaše vyšetrovanie._

_Ďalej by vás spoločnosť Bolt chcela upozorniť, že spracovanie takéhoto množstva údajov, aké ste prevzali, by si vyžiadalo značné množstvo času, čo by viedlo k ďalším oneskoreniam pri poskytovaní požadovaných údajov. Preto ak by ste boli schopní poskytnúť akékoľvek ďalšie údaje, ktoré by spoločnosti Bolt umožnili znížiť množstvo zdieľaných údajov, mohli by sme potom vašu žiadosť spracovať rýchlejšie._

_Radi by sme zopakovali, že všetky údaje, ktoré spoločnosť Bolt zdieľa, sa musia poskytovať v súlade s nariadením GDPR, a preto všetky poskytnuté údaje musia byť nevyhnutné, relevantné a primerané žiadosti, ktorú podávate. Hi [~accountid:5c94f3fc8c3aae2d15117752]!

Our current aim with OPS is to make these articles useful for the users - our top 3 ATI are users reaching out to us regarding received fines, and there is a lot of confusion on the topic. Users don’t generally go to T&C the first thing they have an issue, and it’s difficult to find the info in the long document, hence they reach out to CS.

# Users don’t understand that the fine will be sent to them by the police physically, they think the 30€ admin fee we share in-app is the actual fine.
# The 30€ admin fee wording’s headline states it’s the “parking fee”, hence the additional confusion.

We’re in the process of adding more options for adding fines in the admin, but meanwhile, it would really help us decrease the incoming volumes for Germany.

As an example, Miles (the biggest carsharing player in DE) has similar info in their articles:

[https://support.miles-mobility.com/hc/en-us/articles/4403828547346-I-have-received-a-parking-ticket-What-happens-now-|https://support.miles-mobility.com/hc/en-us/articles/4403828547346-I-have-received-a-parking-ticket-What-happens-now-|smart-link]

HI

This is the result of the dynamic commission, the calculation of monthly commission does this way that  we are taking less commission from the driver because we are subtracting from the total Fee (App orders) - all bonuses/compensations/ride discounts

To calculate ride discounts ( need to export all orders for the same period and calculated the difference between the client payed and the ride price)

This is due to a new invoicing system we gradually started to adopt in mid-2022 called Dynamic Commission. Drivers' or Fleets' bonuses are now aggregated in their commission and the final sum is displayed only as one row: commission row. For example;

Commission: 100€, Bonuses 25€, Booking Fee 15€, Refunds 10€

Driver will only see a single row in their commission invoice in the amount of 50€ (100-25-15-10).

So, technically [actual commission - bounses/compensations - rider discounts - booking fees = commission on the invoice]

the report show the gross commission (the report shows the commission before all these discounts). on the invoice, the amount is all other things deducted from it (since commission netting is active).

More info about dynamic commission [here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/3663265890].

So the monthly invoice will be a source of truth, please note the monthly invoice will not match the weekly report, Report is just a weekly  indicator for the fleet or driver

Hello [~accountid:712020:341b8095-1e4f-44ea-ad93-e6b03a07da4c] , good afternoon,

Below you can see the comments I also posted in the original document.

* Please don’t use “Personally Identifiable Information” or its acronym (PII). The correct legal term is “personal data”, and this is reinforced in our internal training on data protection (“Introduction to Data Protection”). This is so because what’s considered as PII isn’t the same as personal data (the concept of “personal data” is broader than the concept of PII).
* Section “Personal Information”: Actually, in this context (unauthorized copying of data), there’s no risk of a data breach - it really is a data breach. Since the situation covered by this policy may involve a breach of personal data, in which the confidentiality, integrity and/or availability of personal data is compromised, if the employee copies personal data, a specific analysis must be carried out by the DPO or Privacy Legal Team in order to analyze whether or not a notification to the Data Protection Authority is necessary - and if so, the notification must be made within 72 hours. Hence the importance of reinforcing the undesirability of copying personal data. My suggestion is to change the text saying something like "If the data copied is personal data, there is a data breach and the DPO Team must be involved as soon as the copy occurs. In addition, a ticket should be opened by using the Help Center…"
* Please change the link the Privacy Legal Team ticketing system to [https://taxify.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/47/group/157.|https://taxify.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/47/group/157.]
* Section “Strict Intellectual Property violations”: Quick question: wouldn’t our main asset be (personal) data?

I didn't include this next comment in the original document, which is: what practical action will be taken with regard to any data that is copied? I think this needs to be made a little more explicit in the document.

Of course there is an indication of the need to delete the data, but here we have some implications in terms of data protection: even if the employee has infringed any of our internal policy(ies) (or even any legislation), we have to process the (former) employee's personal data in a way that protects such data.

Following on from what [~accountid:712020:0b1ccfcb-3809-460a-88ab-c96985ba329a] suggested: for example, if it is indeed a former employee, or an employee who has resigned, we can probably ask for the person's consent for the deletion situation to take place, since we will inevitably be gaining access to a drive (physical or virtual) that must have its privacy guaranteed.

On the other hand, if the person is still an employee, consent probably can't be used due to the lack of balance between the parties (employer/employee) - and in this case, the Privacy Legal Team must be consulted before any action to access the drive takes place (let alone actions to erase the data).

We understand how sensitive a possible delay in deleting data can be in this type of situation, but we must ensure that these points are met to avoid any kind of backlash from non-compliant employees.

If you need further clarification, please let us know so that we can organize a call. Thank you!

In anthropology there’s a concept of High-context and Low-context cultures. 

In high-context cultures all non-verbal expressions are required to understand full picture of communication. In a situation where users have choice between making a call and writing text message they would prefer making a call instead.

On the opposite side there are so called “Low-context cultures” where information exchange is more direct without the need to contain all additional context information. In such cases, usually users prefer short communication forms like text.

[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High-context_and_low-context_cultures|https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High-context_and_low-context_cultures|smart-link]

I noticed that [~accountid:641d5e830e6828ab20269e6d] specifically asked me to deal with the following comment from the [document|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-ZJb66nxTKVWqY6lUdsvJsYfd8WOR_lsZsz8Z4yws2c/edit]: 

{color:#bf2600}_“NB! According to the 26.09.23 updated meeting notes (here:_ {color}[{color:#bf2600}_https://docs.google.com/document/d/13i4_oAuKRzgdt8Uq4HkF45kYKNnh0GhKMVEhhU5Tz5I/edit?usp=sharing_{color}|https://docs.google.com/document/d/13i4_oAuKRzgdt8Uq4HkF45kYKNnh0GhKMVEhhU5Tz5I/edit?usp=sharing]{color:#bf2600}_) Marketing & Growth teams also want to do cross-promo where not only Bolt Food platform users are targeted, but also ride-hailing users are targeted. Although platform is the one in both cases (operated by Bolt Operations OÜ), then could there be any privacy related issues with cross-targeting?”_{color}

As I have just joined Bolt, I decided to deduct the answer from the user journey that I can take myself. After registering for Bolt Food and exploring, I can identify the following problems:

1] Upon the registration for the Bolt Food app, I am presented with the legal page reference leading to [this page|https://food.bolt.eu/en-US/legal]. If I check the Privacy Policy - it does not mention Bolt Market, and the purposes for data processing are “_To deliver our services to you (lawful basis: to perform and fulfil our contracts with you)_”, where contract is the reference to the ToS. 

2]  If I check the [ToS|https://static.food.bolt.eu/legalDocument/7w4fxF23vgSkBM74Ax0yyy/V5%20of%20Bolt-Client%20T%26C%20(EST)%20-ENG-%20-clean-.pdf], *I find no reference to Bolt Market whatsoever*, but I find the following disclaimer:

_“By operating the Bolt Food Platform and the Marketplace, Bolt_ *_acts only as a provider of the information society service_* _and is neither a party to the Sales Agreement or the Delivery Agreement._ *_Bolt is not the manufacturer or seller of the Goods_* _or provider of the delivery services and is not liable in any way for the performance of the Sales Agreement or the Delivery Agreement.”_

To remind, Bolt is the reference to the Bolt OU entity, and Goods are any goods that the Partner offers for sale through the Bolt Food Platform.

I could not find any other reference to Bolt Market product to identify who operates the product and what are the terms, but of course, being a part of Bolt Food app and subject to the ToS, it should be operated by Bolt OU. Also, the [page|https://bolt.eu/en/food/market/] promoting Bolt Market is protected under Bolt OU copyright, and there are no legal references too.

*3] Based on the above, we can understand the following:*

i)  There is a clear contradiction in the ToS re/ the status of Bolt OU.

ii) The user is not properly informed of the purposes of processing with regard to Bolt Market, as there is no proper reference in the ToS.

iii) Also, the user was not provided with any other meaningful information on Bolt Market that would allow us to assume that we could rely on opt out consent to promote the Bolt Market products.

*4] However, IMO (from the privacy POV:*

if the ToS and the PP are fixed, references to Bolt Market added, and there is meaningful information provided to the user of the Bolt Food App to assume their opt out consent - the Bolt Food customer would essentially be the customer of Bolt Market - which means - there is no problem with cross-targeting. Bolt would be able to promote both Bolt Market and Bolt Food - operated by a single controller, with essentially no data sharing from the privacy point of view.

As said, this is the view from just one angle that I explored - but I believe it raises enough concerns.

This is the result of the dynamic commission, the calculation of monthly commission does this way that we are taking less commission from the driver because we are subtracting from the total Fee (App orders) - all bonuses/compensations/ride discounts

To calculate ride discounts ( need to export all orders for the same period and calculated the difference between the client payed and the ride price)

This is due to a new invoicing system we gradually started to adopt in 1 of October in Azerbaijan called Dynamic Commission. Drivers' or Fleets' bonuses are now aggregated in their commission and the final sum is displayed only as one row: commission row. For example;

Commission: 100€, Bonuses 25€, Booking Fee 15€, Refunds 10€

Driver will only see a single row in their commission invoice in the amount of 50€ (100-25-15-10).

So, technically [actual commission - bounses/compensations - rider discounts - booking fees = commission on the invoice]

the report show the gross commission (the report shows the commission before all these discounts). on the invoice, the amount is all other things deducted from it (since commission netting is active).

More info about dynamic commission [here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/3663265890].

Also, all the records can be found in the [record page|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/billing-rides/records?recordFilter=%7B%22action_timestamp_from%22%3A1697058000%2C%22action_timestamp_to%22%3A1697144399%2C%22from_agent_type%22%3A%22fleet%22%2C%22from_agent_id%22%3A85036%2C%22agent_filter_operator%22%3A%22OR%22%2C%22to_agent_type%22%3A%22fleet%22%2C%22to_agent_id%22%3A85036%7D&page=%7B%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22limit%22%3A100%7D]

So from now on, it will be only 1 row on monthly invoices

Hello Carla,

I'd like to inform you that the updates to the ZAF Annual Vacation system are now in production.

Previously, our time-off plan followed the calendar year, running from January to December, with a carryover period of 6 months, also aligned with the calendar year. 

However, this arrangement did not comply with the carryover regulations mandated in South Africa. In South Africa, employees are required to have a carryover period determined by their anniversary date. As you may recall, previously, everyone's carryover would expire in July, irrespective of their anniversary date.

Now, your annual leave balances have been adjusted to conform with South African local laws. This transition involves changing from a "calendar year" to an "anniversary year" format. With this change, your balances were recalculated based on your anniversary period. 

In your case, not much has changed, as your anniversary period is from January to January and then add 6 months of carryover. Your carryover expires on July 1st then.

You can also check the report called ‘Time Off Results by Period’ (place the name of the report in the search bar and check it). Here’s the guideline on how to read the report: [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/BILP/pages/4578444168/Absence+in+Workday#How-to-read-Time-Off-Balances|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/BILP/pages/4578444168/Absence+in+Workday#How-to-read-Time-Off-Balances|smart-link]

h3. {color:#36b37e}CSAT & AHT Correlation with Refunds{color}

*CSAT*

* Data clearly shows that the more orders end up with a refund, the higher the CSAT is. That totally makes sense, because the main (most probably the only) expected outcome for the riders who contact CS with the _“I was charged more than expected”_ issue, is to receive a refund.

!Screenshot 2023-10-19 at 11.15.09.png|width=33.33333333333333%!

*Handling time*

* In most markets with low handling time, the amount of refunds is high, and that is an indicator that refunding more saves the handling time. I also saw proof of that while reviewing the tickets:
** :green_circle: *Latvia & Lithuania* are giving quick refunds, if they see the overcharge and a clear reason for it, they simply refund without asking additional questions and completing further investigations.
** 🔴 *Thailand & Nigeria* perform additional, unnecessary actions, such as clarifying a lot of details with the rider, contacting the driver, negotiating with the rider about refund amount, etc. Also, their amount of refunds is low because they are asking the driver to make a money transfer to the rider, they are not refunding themselves, and these are also irrelevant, undocumented actions.
* *Interesting to check:*
** How did Ukraine and Azerbaijan manage to keep the handling time low with a relatively small amount of refunds?
** What influences high handling time in Estonia, if they solved 64% of cases with refunds?

About the booking fee please check this [article|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/1709050132/Booking+Fees] hope it will make it clear.

About the fleer the report, basically, it is an overview of the driver's orders in gross like a dashboard. (as we do not have access to this, you can check this with the local team, they can explain more detail about that)

The calculation of monthly commission does this way that  we are taking less commission from the driver because we are subtracting from the total Fee (App orders) - all bonuses/compensations/ride discounts

To calculate ride discounts ( need to export all orders for the same period and calculated the difference between the client payed and the ride price)

This is due to a new invoicing system we gradually started to adopt in mid-2022 called Dynamic Commission. Drivers' or Fleets' bonuses are now aggregated in their commission and the final sum is displayed only as one row: commission row. For example;

Commission: 100€, Bonuses 25€, Booking Fee 15€, Refunds 10€

Driver will only see a single row in their commission invoice in the amount of 50€ (100-25-15-10).

So, technically [actual commission - bounses/compensations - rider discounts - booking fees = commission on the invoice]

the report show the gross commission (the report shows the commission before all these discounts). on the invoice, the amount is all other things deducted from it (since commission netting is active).

More info about dynamic commission [here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/3663265890].

So if the rider requests to reissue the invoice for their own sake in the future, +you can tell them+ +*according to art., 106b ust. 6 VAT law in Poland*++, we are not allowed to do so.+

{noformat}WITH reported_by_system AS (
	SELECT 
		tw.id, 
		sic.created,
		(CASE WHEN tw.safety_severity_level IN ('minor', 'severe', 'critical') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS solved_as_safety,
		(CASE WHEN sic.aggregate IN ('minor', 'severe', 'critical') AND sic.agent_indicator IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS reported_as_safety_by_system,
		(CASE WHEN sic.aggregate IN ('minor', 'severe', 'critical') AND sic.agent_indicator IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS reported_as_safety_by_agent,
		(CASE WHEN sic.agent_indicator IS NULL AND sic.aggregate = 'none' THEN 0
		     WHEN sic.agent_indicator IS NULL AND sic.aggregate = 'minor' THEN 1
		     WHEN sic.agent_indicator IS NULL AND sic.aggregate = 'severe' THEN 2
		     WHEN sic.agent_indicator IS NULL AND sic.aggregate = 'critical' THEN 3
		     ELSE 0 END) AS severity_level_by_system,
		(CASE WHEN sic.agent_indicator IS NOT NULL AND sic.aggregate = 'none' THEN 0
		     WHEN sic.agent_indicator IS NOT NULL AND sic.aggregate = 'minor' THEN 1
		     WHEN sic.agent_indicator IS NOT NULL AND sic.aggregate = 'severe' THEN 2
		     WHEN sic.agent_indicator IS NOT NULL AND sic.aggregate = 'critical' THEN 3
		     ELSE 0 END) AS severity_level_by_agent
	FROM ng_customer_support.etl_tw_support_case AS tw
	LEFT JOIN customer_support.support_case_safety_indicator_changed AS sic ON tw.id = sic.support_case_id 
	WHERE tw.created > DATE('2023-09-01') AND tw.state = 'closed'
	ORDER BY sic.created ASC
),
safety_indicator_per_case AS (
	SELECT 
		id, 
		MAX(solved_as_safety) AS solved_as_safety, 
		MAX(reported_as_safety_by_system) AS reported_as_safety_by_system,
		MAX(reported_as_safety_by_agent) AS reported_as_safety_by_agent,
		MAX(severity_level_by_system) AS severity_level_by_system,
		MAX(severity_level_by_agent) AS severity_level_by_agent
	FROM reported_by_system
	GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT 
	id,
	solved_as_safety,
	(CASE WHEN reported_as_safety_by_system = 1 AND reported_as_safety_by_agent = 0 THEN 1
	      WHEN reported_as_safety_by_system = 1 AND reported_as_safety_by_agent = 1 AND severity_level_by_agent > severity_level_by_system THEN 1
	      ELSE 0 END) AS reported_as_safety_by_system
FROM safety_indicator_per_case
LIMIT 1000;{noformat}

Here is the query to get safety data. Notice that safety indicator table consists of both automated as well as manual ways to set safety labels, so there is specific logic to understand reported safety cases. In general current results are much better than what we used to expect before (i.e. precision 0.42 vs 0.2 and recall 0.6 vs 0.4). Potential improvements might be coming from language specific keywords.

Scheduled orders.

Finding scheduled orders:

{noformat}select *
from core_models_spark.fact_rides_order_try
where created_date = date('2023-08-01')
and order_key in (select order_key from core_models_spark.fact_rides_order where order_type = 'scheduled' and created_date >= date('2023-07-25'))
limit 10{noformat}

Example

!image-20231020-063432.png|width=626,height=755!

(/) fact_rides_order - order gets added on 2023-07-30, when calculating metrics based on order table, this will get included on 2023-07-30

(/) fact_rides_order_try - order try gets added on 2023-08-01, order data gets added because we include up to 30 days of order data when doing the join, when calculating metrics based on order try table, the metrics will get included into 2023-08-01

(/) mart_city_date - order based metrics will be added on 2023-07-30 into 2023-07-30, order try based metrics will be added on 2023-08-01 into order try

(!) mart_rides_orders - if we only include data from data_interval

* on 2023-07-30 we will add the order into mart_rides_orders and it will have orders_created=1 and orders_finished=0 and all order_try based metrics like gmv, distance etc equal to 0
* on 2023-08-01 we will have a new row appearing where order try based metrics are filled, but all the attribute fields from order table are blank because we are not including order data from the appropriate date?

Calculation date 2023-08-01, include 30 days of data from all tables:

* will include this order try, will include this order, row will be complete, can overwrite previously written row where orders_created was 1 and orders_finished was 0
* will include another order try from 29 days ago, this will have orders_finished = 1, but order attributes empty

If I include dimension order_try_key__order_created_date then I can limit the final output of data mart to order_try_key__order_created_date >= calculation date - 30 days. This will limit the data that will get overwritten to only these orders that have complete data in this calculation. 

Cannot include order_try_key__order_created_date because this is not a valid dimension for metrics coming from order table.

Limiting the output data based on order_key__created_date should do the same trick.

Hey [~accountid:619df385ef18ca00711f4974] we have just received the following reply from AGA:

* The service provider mentioned under question 3(c) of the form only covers services that have transactions on the digital platform or are relevant to the digital platform, not the company. For instance, the officer cited a payment portal as an example. Under this section, law consulting firms and accounting firms are not applicable since they provide services to the company, not the digital platform.
* The "value of transactions that occurred on the digital platform" under question 2(d) refers to the total amount of money flowing into the platforms. For instance, it would mean total income from passengers in the case of Bolt. On the other hand, "income before deducting expenses from providing digital platform services in the kingdom" under question 2(e) refers to the revenue that the platform earns before deducting business costs. In the context of Bolt, it would mean total commission fees that remain after paying drivers but before deducting other business expenses such as local staff salaries and platform maintenance.
* B2B businesses are accounted for and need to be reported only if the transaction occurs through the digital platform. Direct billing from one company to another is not considered, as the transaction is not conducted through the digital platform and it is counted as the company's transaction, not the platform's.
* If a platform operates multiple verticals, such as food-delivery, ride-hailing, and marketplace, the officer confirmed that it's acceptable to report them on the same form. However, they suggested using different forms because it might impact whether the platform is classified as a large or specified platform or not. The criteria for these classifications include metrics like revenue and the number of average monthly active users (AMAU). Since Bolt only has a ride-hailing business at the moment, Bolt should use one form.
* As we had attempted to notify through the Digital Portal, but encountered issues with the next step button on the first page. The ETDA suspects that the problem arises when using a personal ID number. They recommended using a corporate ID number for the notification. However, they've acknowledged this issue and plan to consult their team for resolution. Additionally, they mentioned that the English version of the subordinate laws is currently under approval. They will release it soon by the notification deadline.

Having a closer look at the issue, here are my thoughts (as discussed previously during the call):

1] As Pixels do not store data on a user's device like cookies, and instead, they send data to a remote server, the consent requirement of the ePrivacy Directive should not apply:

_“Users should have the opportunity to refuse to have a cookie or similar device stored on their terminal equipment.”_

IMO, this should allow us to rely on legitimate interest, and an LIA will have to be conducted.

2] As for the preliminary risk assessment - there were some problems:

* _the possibility to halt the processing of data - answered with no_ - however, I believe it is strictly necessary to be able to halt the processing, e.g., under the request of the DS.
* _data retention - its indicated the the deletion was not planned_ - I believe data retention period should be established. As a compromise, “until the purpose of processing ceases to exist can be indicated”, and after Bolt is done with the activity, the data can be anonymised. 

3] Apart from the considerations above, we will have to:

* check the agreements with Presto (as I am sure for Amazon there has to be an agreement)
* transparency - IMO, Privacy Policy should be the main source of transparency re/ this activity, and not Cookie Policy - as we have established that cookies and pixels are fundamentally different technologies.

Please let me know your thoughts.

At Courier OPS, we monitor both types of failed orders: those involving Couriers and Bolt at fault, as those are solely related to courier issues. We do this because failed orders with the actor at fault Bolt usually happen when we're unable to assign an order to a courier. This is usually due to a supply problem where we can't find a suitable courier to handle the order, or our pricing isn't attractive enough, leading couriers to reject the orders.

As CS can manually fail the orders, it is extremely important for us to have reliable data and an aligned process for the orders where the courier or Bolt is at fault. Currently, I see that often orders are manually failed with Courier or Bolt at fault, even though it was the eater cancellation or other issues not related to both of these actors.

I will give you a couple of examples, but I can share hundreds of them if needed:

[https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/delivery-order/orders/140558215?shard=deliveryglobal&pricingEaterTab=fee_components|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/delivery-order/orders/140558215?shard=deliveryglobal&pricingEaterTab=fee_components] 

* Admin: Anna Berga Reason: E wants to cancel the order, P not answering

In this case, specifically, R is saying that they didn’t change the destination (we can see that they, for some reason, booked a round trip, but only went one way). Due to R’s mistake, D suffers a loss because a higher commission is charged.

The estimated price was 181kr and after the destination changed, which was not reached, [it increased to 733kr|https://europe-admin.bolt.eu/order/PricePredictions/all/1384449094/1581303787].

After recalculating the price, I get ~400kr. So the overcharge is 384kr, which should be refunded to the rider with the driver as the actor.

If we follow the destination not reached article and refund the overcharge, D suffers a loss. They should have gotten 749kr - 23% commission (172kr) = 577kr; however, D only got 365kr (the final price minus the overcharge, 733kr-384kr) - the commission from the incorrect final price, 172kr. So they receive the net payment of 193kr. 

The correct commission from 400kr should be 92kr. So we should compensate the driver 172kr - 92kr = 80kr.

This ticket was handled incorrectly (no compensation to R), and the rider was overcharged due to the destination change that was not reached.

# It is necessary to have a procedure, so agents can handle such tickets correctly.

{noformat}with balance_entry as
(
     select
          currency,
          entity_type,
          entity_id,
          transaction_type,
          transaction_subtype,
          case when transaction_type = 'payout' then cast(balance_local_date as timestamp) else cast(balance_local_date as timestamp) + interval '1' hour  end as created_date,
          cast(sum(amount) as decimal(38,5)) as amount
     from ng_public.etl_billing_balance_driver_v2 etl
     where etl.balance_local_date < DATE('2023-10-09')
     group by 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6
),
balance_summary as
(
     select
     *,
     sum(amount) over(partition by entity_id, currency, entity_type order by created_date asc rows between unbounded preceding and current row) as current_balance
     from balance_entry
),
earnings as (
select
DATE(balance_local_date) as date,
entity_id,
entity_type,
currency,
sum(amount) as daily_sum,
sum(case when transaction_type in ('ride_fee','ride_cash_payment') then amount end) as net_earnings
from ng_public.etl_billing_balance_driver_v2 
where balance_local_date < DATE('2023-10-09')
and transaction_type != 'payout'
group by 1,2,3,4
),
payouts as (
select
date_trunc('week', balance_local_date) as week,
entity_id,
entity_type,
etl.currency,
sum(amount) as payout
from ng_public.etl_billing_balance_driver_v2 etl
where balance_local_date < DATE('2023-10-09')
and transaction_type = 'payout'
and amount < 0
group by 1,2,3,4
), 
summary as (
select 
bs.*,
e.daily_sum,
e.net_earnings,
p.payout as weekly_payout
from balance_summary bs
left join earnings e on e.entity_id = bs.entity_id and e.entity_type = bs.entity_type and e.date = DATE(bs.created_date)
left join payouts p on p.entity_id = bs.entity_id and p.entity_type = bs.entity_type and date_trunc('week', bs.created_date) = (p.week - interval '7' day)
where p.payout is not null
and e.daily_sum > 0
), summary2 as (
select 
currency,
entity_id,
entity_type,
transaction_type,
transaction_subtype,
date_trunc('day', created_date) as date,
weekly_payout,
daily_sum,
sum(amount) as type_sum
from summary s 
group by 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8
), summary3 as (
select * ,
sum(case when daily_sum > 0 and type_sum > 0 then type_sum else 0 end) over(partition by currency,entity_id, entity_type, date_trunc('week', date)) as weekly_pos_sum,
type_sum/sum(case when daily_sum > 0 and type_sum > 0 then type_sum else 0 end) over(partition by currency,entity_id, entity_type, date_trunc('week', date)) as type_rate
from summary2
where type_sum >0
), summary4 as (
select 
ic.country,
s.currency,
entity_type,
entity_id,
date_trunc('week', date) as week,
transaction_type,
transaction_subtype,
sum(type_rate) as type_rate
from summary3 s
left join ng_public.invoicing_client ic on ic.external_id = s.entity_id and ic.type = case when s.entity_type = 'driver' then 'Driver' else 'Company' end
group by 1,2,3,4,5,6,7
)
select 
s.country,
s.currency,
s.entity_type,
s.week,
s.transaction_type,
s.transaction_subtype,
avg(type_rate) as avg_rate,
sum(avg(type_rate)) over(partition by s.country, currency, entity_type, week) as weekly_rate,
avg(s.type_rate)/sum(avg(s.type_rate)) over(partition by s.country, s.currency, s.entity_type, s.week) as rate_norm
from summary4 s
where s.week >= DATE('2023-06-01') 
and s.week < DATE('2023-10-01')
group by 1,2,3,4,5,6{noformat}

Hi [~accountid:62b2cf2c99eafa602d88ec9e] 

After having assessed the issue in more detail, we have the following conclusions.

i) this idea would require a thorough assessment of obligations under the PCI DSS framework, which Bolt is subject to. This standard is very strict, and requirements such as encryption at rest and various infosec protection measures should be in place for card payment data, including IINs. Any handling, storage, processing, or transmission of the IIN falls within the scope of PCI DSS and Bolt must adhere to its requirements to ensure the protection of this sensitive data.

Consequently, *a more thorough assessment of our obligations under PCI DSS from a specialist, and involvement of the infosec to make sure other PCI DSS requirements are met for the activity will be required.*

ii) in addition to PCI DSS considerations, substantial work (10-15 hours) from the privacy team to legalise the activity will have to be done - if there is green light for the p.1.

iii) Bolt recently prepared a corporate public statements, where we explicitly mention not to be storing payment data on our servers - and I believe, if we proceed with this activity, it will be processed on our servers. So, if we proceed with the activity, this will contradict our public stance, and likely it could not be adjusted for this specific activity.

So, in the light of the above, we believe it would not be possible to go forward with the activity.



Also, could you please clarify what you meant by Issuer “_Identification Number (IIN) - which is saved and stored already)” -_ because if it is on our servers, this means we are in breach of our undertakings.

Also fyi - IINs are a part of PAN (Primary Account Number), and certainly falls under the PCI DSS.

Hi [~accountid:62c57c181bb561c33795cdc2] 

It might be possible due to a day-end ride, usually, the orders finished at midnight are added to the next day’s balance, as the balance calculation is based on the time stamp.

This causes a time difference between the payout system and the balance system. However, the balance and the payout is correct. It is only a discrepancy in the reporting. Most importantly they have received this difference in the next payout.

Please check the new [view balance|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/user-balance/balance?filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A25%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%22start_date_ts%22%3A1696197600%2C%22end_date_ts%22%3A1696802400%2C%22types%22%3A%5B%22ride_hailing_fleet%22%5D%2C%22external_id%22%3A67889%7D%7D&tz=Europe%2FTallinn] to check the correctness of the payout.

And please check the [record|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/billing-rides/records?recordFilter=%7B%22action_timestamp_from%22%3A1696197600%2C%22action_timestamp_to%22%3A1696802400%2C%22from_agent_type%22%3A%22fleet%22%2C%22from_agent_id%22%3A67889%2C%22agent_filter_operator%22%3A%22OR%22%2C%22to_agent_type%22%3A%22fleet%22%2C%22to_agent_id%22%3A67889%7D&page=%7B%22limit%22%3A100%2C%22offset%22%3A0%7D] of the end days of Sunday (in this example will be a different timezone because of my location)


!Screenshot 2023-10-20 at 16.10.02.png|width=1624,height=544!

This is the cause of the day-end order, the record was created on 09.10 at 01:05 (your time will be 00:05)but the time stamp is for the previous day so that is why sometimes reflected in the reports ( as some report still pick data from admin v1)

Hi [~accountid:712020:47b28358-3e16-42e1-98f8-60975dca1fc0] 

We have now assessed possible courses of action in relation to this issue, based on the informative document that you sent us and the master agreement (referred to as the 'agreement' below). 

First, please note that based on experience with contract performance reviews and similar disputes, the most fruitful way of solving this issue is usually to have a sit-down and try to find common ground. Therefore, I recommend considering how the below assessment can be used it as basis for negotiation with Skagstind rather than for taking legal action. +In any event, please note that the legal team does not recommend sending any further communication to Skagstind without running it by us first at this stage.+

*Executive summary*

We agree that Skagstind seems to have committed one or several breaches of its obligations under the agreement. Our assessment is that this entitles Bolt to a few different options in terms of actions moving forward, including termination with immediate effect and/or claiming compensation from Skagstind for their underperformance. We recommend approaching this through negotiations rather than legal proceedings (in court) at this stage. Please find the grounds for our assessment in further detail below.

*The purpose of the agreement and Skagstind’s obligations*

The purpose of the agreement is, according to clause 1: “to promote the brand of Bolt”. As expressed by you in the performance review document, we agree that Skagstind has not lived up to reasonable expectations in this sense. To fulfil the purpose of the agreement, Skagstind has undertaken certain obligations, including:

* According to clause 4.4 and 4.5 of the agreement, Skagstind has agreed to provide access to the marketing channels, and ensure that the necessary tools and resources are made available to Bolt so that Bolt can effectively utilise the marketing channels and reach its target audiences, as necessary to fulfil the purpose (to promote the Bolt brand).
* From what we understand, Skagstind has made certain commitments in Appendix A, for example, with respect to specific amounts and types of stickers, posters, coasters, screens, etc. Provided that such targets were included in Attachment A when the agreement was signed, any failure to meet them is considered breach of contract, too.

*Has Skagstind committed any breach of contract?*

Based on the information you provided in the performance review document, Skagstind seems to be in breach of several of its obligations under the agreement. For example, the manner in which the promotional material has been used in Skagstind’s venues is not putting Bolt in a good light, which is contrary to the purpose of the agreement, and should be deemed a breach of contract. Skagstind may also have failed to meet certain defined targets in Attachment A, in which case such failures should each be considered a breach as well. 

Depending on the severity of the breach or breaches, Bolt may be entitled to different remedies under the agreement, including the right to terminate the agreement with immediate effect and/or the right to claim direct damages. 

*Right for Bolt to terminate the agreement due to breach of contract*

_Termination due to material breach clause 3a)_ 

Clause 3a) of the agreement allows Bolt to terminate the agreement with immediate effect if Skagstind commits a material breach of its obligations under the agreement. It is required that Bolt gives Skagstind 10 days prior written notice, specifying what the material breach consists of, and stating that Bolt wishes to terminate the agreement on this ground. Unless Skagstind manages to rectify the breach within the next 10 days of receiving notice, the agreement is automatically terminated thereafter. *Please do* +*not*+ *send any further communication* at this point, but has Bolt _already_ expressed any wish to terminate the agreement to Skagstind? 

_Is the breach material?_

To be legally entitled to terminate the agreement with immediate effect based on clause 3a) as mentioned above, Bolt must be able to show that Skagstind has committed a material breach of contract. Based on the details regarding the collaboration so far provided in the performance review document, my assessment is that Skagstind may be considered to have committed one or several material breaches of the agreement, and Bolt should therefore be entitled to terminate the agreement.

Undermining the purpose of the agreement may be considered a material breach of contract. As an example, putting up stickers randomly all around restaurants, _particularly_ on trash bins, not only fails to effectively promote Bolt’s brand to its target audiences, it may actually +undermine+ the brand’s credibility and have +negative+ effects on goodwill. Such effects would reasonably be the opposite of the intention with the agreement, which is why this alone _should_ be enough to evidence a material breach.

Also, failure to meet any agreed targets, e.g., that there are no beer coasters, no wall posters, that the table stickers are not placed as agreed, and that the majority of the venues lack the agreed digital presence of the Bolt brand, may either separately or weighed together make up to a material breach of contract.

Further, it could perhaps be argued that the short contract term increases the severity of Skagstind’s breaches. Since time is so particularly of the essence in this agreement, any time devoted to a breach of contract (and remedy) may significantly reduce the total value of the agreement for Bolt. It may not even be remedied before the agreement term expires.

*Right for Bolt to claim direct damages due to breach of contract*

According to clause 9 of the agrement, Skagstind is liable to Bolt for any direct damages incurred as a result of a material breach of Skagstind’s obligations under the agreement. This means that Bolt can claim damages corresponding to its losses that have arisen due to one or several specific breaches by Skagstind. To claim direct damages based on breach of contract, Bolt must be able to prove that Bolt has suffered a loss _as a direct consequence_ of the relevant breach/breaches. It may be difficult to calculate an exact amount, however, if you believe that it’s possible to calculate precisely in this case, please let us know and we can assess whether we think we can move forward with it from a legal perspective.

*Other remedies available to Bolt*

Regardless of any legal obstacles with respect to claiming direct damages in court, my assessment is that we may be able to claim a _refund_, which can be _based on the argument that we are entitled to damages,_ as the underperformance by Skagstind is so severe that the contract is wholly or partially useless to us. In other words, we could argue that the money spent on this contract, either all of it or a part of it, was a direct loss in itself, since the purpose has been undermined. 

It is _always_ possible to negotiate what would be a reasonable refund of the contract sum based on Skagstinds non-performance, and our negotiation may be wholly or partially based on the issues brought up in this legal assessment.

*Termination based on the alternative termination-clause 3d)*

In addition to the ground for termination mentioned above, Bolt is also entitled to terminate the agreement with immediate effect if Skagstind “_conducts its business in a way that [Bolt] reasonably considers may undermine the perception of the brand with the public or investors or which may otherwise have a negative impact on goodwill.”_

This ground for termination may also be worth considering, as it does not require a material breach, but rather that Skagstind has conducted its business in a way which may put Bolt in a bad light. Considering that they put stickers on trash bins, specifically with reference to the statement in the performance review “_It all looks incredibly unprofessional, almost as if the whole place has been invaded by a bunch of Bolt football hooligans_.”, it’s an option worth considering.

Termination on this ground can of course be made in combination with negotiation regarding compensation/refund. 

*Do we have to terminate the agreement in order to claim financial compensation from Skagstind?*

No. Regardless of whether we decide to terminate the agreement and/or what grounds for termination we would decide to go with, it is motivated in our assessment to claim some sort of compensation or refund from Skagstind. The argument for this would in essence be that Bolt is very dissatisfied with the outcome of the collaboration, and that Bolt could not have reasonably foreseen that this would be Skagstind’s level of (non-)performance when entering into the agreement.

Hey [~accountid:63d9322adb4f715c971f5c22] To wrap it up here as well following our multiple Slack threads with several badgers 🙂 

* As we don’t have a company held and contracted account for OpenAI products atm (other than for the API arrangement for the CS use case, and the Playground option for low scale testing purposes) then it’s accepted behavior under our [internal policy|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LEG/pages/4496753015/Guidance+on+using+GPT+Assistants] that a badger signs up for a private account for the use of a GPT assistant, accepts the user terms, and prompts the data *while honoring the limits set in the internal policy*.
* Perhaps most importantly it means that only data qualified as for _public_ and _internal_ use should be prompted. But no _restricted_ nor _confidential_ data. Also don’t forget to *consistently disable the option to save history and/or permit the assistant to utilize the entered data for training itself.*

The above said, and considering you need to use a GPT assistant for levelling up the Bolt Business team’s internal training processes and content then:

* prompting Bolt created content to GPT for the latter to generate FAQ for the sales team - fine as long as it’s not restricted or confidential data;
* using content generated by GPT itself for the same internal trainings purposes - fine;
* prompting 3rd party partner’s (Groove, Salesforce etc) content to a GPT assistant for the latter to generate FAQ - fine, *if* we have received respective consent from the 3rd party, or if the content is public anyway. Otherwise we should consider this data as confidential/ not ok to be shared to a 3rd party GPT assistant.

Cheers!

I decided to take some additional time to double check the technical nature of pixels, and having delved deeper, *I found that my previous guidance was not fully correct, as pixels in fact would fall under the ePrivacy Directive.*

To clarify:

# *Technology of Pixels:* A tracking pixel is actually a file downloaded onto the user's device. When a user accesses an email with an embedded pixel, their browser retrieves the img link embedded in the email forcing them to connect to the server to download it to their client. This act, in essence, is storing information on the user's device, even if temporarily.
# *Embedded Code:* Even in scenarios where the pixel is blocked or redirected (e.g., to a 404 error), the embedded code within the email or webpage (the http img element referencing the pixel) remains present on the user's device
# *Consent required:* Given the above, the pixels, considering they are not "strictly necessary" for service provision, would require explicit consent under the ePrivacy Directive.
# Other points from my previous answer (p. 2, 3) - should remain valid.

Currently on the market there are a few free open source engines and a few Cloud based engines available on subscription. 

Free:

* OpenAI Whisper - actively supported [https://github.com/openai/whisper|https://github.com/openai/whisper|smart-link] 
* Facebook MMS - actively supported model [https://github.com/facebookresearch/fairseq/tree/main/examples/mms|https://github.com/facebookresearch/fairseq/tree/main/examples/mms|smart-link] 
* Platform built-in (check if API is open)
* Mozilla DeepSpeech - *abandoned in 2021* [https://github.com/mozilla/DeepSpeech|https://github.com/mozilla/DeepSpeech|smart-link] 
* Coqui-ai STT - *abandoned in 2022* [https://github.com/coqui-ai/STT|https://github.com/coqui-ai/STT|smart-link] 

Payed:

* Amazon Transcribe - [https://aws.amazon.com/pm/transcribe|https://aws.amazon.com/pm/transcribe|smart-link] 
* Microsoft STT - [https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/products/ai-services/speech-to-text|https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/products/ai-services/speech-to-text|smart-link] 
* Google STT - [https://cloud.google.com/speech-to-text|https://cloud.google.com/speech-to-text|smart-link] 
* IBM Watson STT - [https://www.ibm.com/products/speech-to-text|https://www.ibm.com/products/speech-to-text|smart-link] 

Some of the free engines are not maintained by their main developers anymore, but they still can be forked and supported if we are ready to invest in these projects. Reply from the police:

The legal support the Police Authority has for requesting that information is found in Section 2 of the Police Act, where it is stated that the police must investigate and prosecute crimes. The police authority also has legal support according to the Code of Procedure (RB) chapter 23 to investigate a certain crime within the framework of a preliminary investigation, i.e. also request information from the public.

There is also a legal obligation (6.1 c GDPR, 2:1 of the Data Protection Act), and balancing of interests (6.1 f GDPR) that the Police Authority has made that the criminal investigation interest outweighs that of the individual in this case.
