Hey, [~accountid:6151cf6878e5e40070fb74c2]! I received a response from the external counsel. To sum up, statutory provisions in SK are not entirely in line with EU directive and lack logic. Their local act is Act no. 102/2014 Coll. on consumer protection in distance contracts (the “*Act*”). Here is what we need to do in SK by default:

* Provide information as per Article 6(1)(h) of the Directive (*done*)
* Advise according to § 4 par. 6) of the Act (*need to add wording suggested by external counsel in new section 2*)
* Seek express consent to start provision of the service before the end of the withdrawal period as per Article 8 (8) of the Directive. (*need to add a page in the app with a button seeking consent and allow to subscribe even if consent is not given*)
* Ask for a declaration according to § 4 par. 6) of the Act (*need to add a page in the app with a button and certain text*)

{color:#bf2600}*External counsel said that we need to do the things listed above to comply with the local legislation. Non-compliance with the provisions of the local legislation is an administrative offence and a fine for such offence would be between 200 and 10,000 euros.*{color}

If we want to issue a partial refund we need to add in addition to the above a wording in our T&Cs in accordance with Article 6(1)(j) of the Directive (i.e. information that the user will need to compensate Bolt in case some benefits were used prior to withdrawal). The counsel confirmed that there is no need to add the particulars of the calculation of the proportional cost to the T&Cs, but in case this will be checked by the authority or we will have a dispute the burden of proof will lie on us to show that the proportional cost was calculated on the basis of the total price agreed in the contract.

*Conclusion*

Based on the information I gathered from the directive and external counsel here is what I think we need to do in terms of both SK and global version of T&Cs:

*SK version:*

To avoid fines we need to:

* Add suggested new section 2
* Draft and add wording as per Article 6(1)(j) of the Directive for partial refund in T&Cs
* Prepare wording for consent and declaration
* Figure out how to seek consent and declaration



*Global version:*

Based on directive the risk for us of not seeking consent is that we will not be entitled to issue a partial refund and in case we want to issue only full refund it is enough to add information as per Article 6(1)(h) of the Directive to comply with the directive. However, since we want to get partial refund here is what we need to do:

* Draft and add wording as per Article 6(1)(j) of the Directive for partial refund in T&Cs
* Prepare wording of consent as per Article 8 (8) of the Directive and add it to T&Cs or on a separate page in the app (the latter is preferred)


*Next steps*

* I will prepare the ENG and SK version of T&Cs in SK based on the conclusion above. I would like you to review the ENG version. 
* I will then send external counsel SK version for a review. I assume that we can get the SK version reviewed by the end of this week. 
* I suggest that you will ask what can we do about consent and declaration. I can prepare the wording for these.

Hi [~accountid:63fddd1c7655a3223a21b876],

there could be several reasons why the query results may differ between Spark and Presto, for example:

* source tables may not be completely in sync. This can happen especially for recent data, due to various levels of caching.
* your client settings may be different, especially for time zone settings.
* Spark SQL and Presto SQL are not 100% compatible. Especially with such complicated join conditions as in this query, there could easily be some differences that affect the results.

So if the results of such a query are not equivalent, this does not necessarily indicate an issue with the data. If you want to figure out what exactly is causing the difference, you’ll have to break down the query into the individual steps to determine which step is causing the difference.

The police authority may collect and process personal data in order to investigate and prosecute crimes according to ch. 2. 1 § 2 of the Act (2018:1693) on the police's processing of personal data within the scope of the Criminal Data Act.

According to ch. 1, the police authority is Section 4 of the Act on the police's processing of personal data within the area of ​​the Criminal Data Act personal data controller for the processing of personal data carried out by the authority.

Information in an ongoing preliminary investigation is covered by confidentiality in accordance with the provisions in ch. 18. 1 and 35 chap. §§ 1 of the Publicity and Confidentiality Act (2009:400). {noformat}# Calculates the amount of memory to reserve for kubeReserved in mebibytes. KubeReserved is a function of pod
# density so we are calculating the amount of memory to reserve for Kubernetes systems daemons by
# considering the maximum number of pods this instance type supports.
# Args:
#   $1 the max number of pods per instance type (MAX_PODS) based on values from /etc/eks/eni-max-pods.txt
# Return:
#   memory to reserve in Mi for the kubelet
get_memory_mebibytes_to_reserve() {
  local max_num_pods=$1
  memory_to_reserve=$((11 * $max_num_pods + 255))
  echo $memory_to_reserve
}{noformat}

As per the provided definition, a related party of Bolt is: 

(a) A person or a close member of that person’s family is related to a reporting entity if that person:
(i) has control or joint control of the reporting entity;
(ii) has significant influence over the reporting entity; or
(iii) is a member of the key management personnel of the reporting entity or of a parent of the reporting entity.

(i) - has control or joint control - this should be deemed Markus Villig. Under *Estonian law*, control is defined either by way of:

(a) ownership - i.e. direct or indirect (via other holding companies). Under Estonian laws a person is deemed to control a company if he/she owns over 25% of the shares of a company; or

(b) other type of control - e.g. via voting rights (under shareholders' agreement or otherwise). Under Estonian law a person is deemed to control a company if he/she can, for example, appoint the majority of members of the board.

There is no person who directly or indirectly owns over 25% of shares (falling under (a) in the above description).  Markus Villig, through rights given to the founders under Company’s articles of association, has the ultimate right to appoint management board members of the company --> thus *Markus should be deemed having control of Bolt Technology OÜ*.



(ii) - has significant influence - as per our analysis there is no one in Bolt’s organisation who has singificant influence but is not otherwise covered by ( i) or (iii)

(iii) - member of key management personnel - member of key management personnel of Bolt are: 

* CEO Markus Villig
* CFO Mikko Salovaara
* President Jevgeni Kabanov



Definition of related party does not automatically include all members of the management board or members of the supervisory board. Additionally, considering the role of supervisory board members (supervising the activities of management board of company, as set out in the law), the members of the supervisory board do not fall under the definition of related party (having control, otherwise significant influence or being members of key management personnel).

If you have a negative balance -of EUR3 and your cash ride is EUR 13, you still need to pay cash of EUR 10 instead of EUR 13. Your balance will remain unchanged.


2. The amount in the Bolt balance does not expire, it remains intact and untouched until the user is ready to use it.

[~accountid:611b95f747d1df00762c6b63] [~accountid:63a2c00015d69a40aa170e8b] [~accountid:6052891960d39e006f72f0f0] 

In most EU countries the concept of *“income from employment”* provided for by Personal Income Tax (PIT) Laws is larger than the concept of “salary/payroll” provided for by Labour Law. Therefore, if we pay out *monetary incentives* (i.e. bonuses) to couriers such an income may qualify as income from employment for the couriers’ PIT purposes. Under such a scenario, *Bolt may become liable to withhold taxes on such an income*. This topic should be addressed country by country to ensure (i) whether such a qualification applies and (ii) the amounts that would have to be withheld by Bolt and settled before the local tax authorities.

On top of the above, In some countries (i.e. Spain) the Labor Authorities may take advantage of the aforementioned qualification of income to seek for reclassification of couriers into Bolt employees locally or, at least, this issue could provide them with an extra argument to challenge the couriers' status for labor law purposes.

*What extra cost would for example a promo code that is worth 100€ carry?* _It depends on the withholding tax (WHT) rate provided for by the tax law of each one of the countries where we mean to launch the campaign._

*If we want to gift couriers for example 50€ gift cards from Apollo Cinemas for example, do they also qualify for this?*

_If we grant cards for Apollo Cinemas as a consideration for the couriers’ delivery work, such a gift may qualify as income from employment paid in kind. Bolt may be liable to bear the withholding tax cost that should apply to such a benefit in kind._

_If we merely give such cards as a gift, not related to the delivery work, the cost of such cards would not qualify as a tax-deductible cost for Bolts’ Corporate Tax purposes, so Bolt would have to bear (i) the cost of the items given as gifts, (ii) the Corporate tax due associated to such a cost and (iii) the input VAT borne by Bolt from the purchase of the items given as gifts._

*We have done them also in the past so I would like to understand the difference here?* _I’m afraid I cannot provide an answer to this question, as I only took over from Tiiu a couple of weeks ago. Perhaps the economic impact of former campaigns was non-material so the tax cost that arose from those campaigns would be non-material as well, or perhaps there were circumstances leading to a different approach._

*We want to organize an appreciation month for couriers that has certain monetary gifts involved to show our extra appreciation. I don't see how giving promo codes VS order qtd based bonuses is any different?*

_If you could provide me with a business case I may be able to provide an assessment of the tax cost that may arise from such a monthly campaign. If you can, please let me know the scope of the campaign (EE only?, Baltics only?, Europe?, etc) and the expected cost of the items to be given as a gift (country by country)._

Thanks a lot and have a good day.

Hi [~accountid:63a00e3e6ad11358a0962398] 

Please take note that the commission in the monthly invoice will never match with the report.

This is the result of the dynamic commission, the calculation of monthly commission does this way that  we are taking less commission from the driver because we are subtracting from the total Fee (App orders) - all bonuses/compensations/ride discounts

To calculate ride discounts ( need to export all orders for the same period and calculated the difference between the client payed and the ride price)

This is due to a new invoicing system we gradually started to adopt in mid-2022 called Dynamic Commission. Drivers' or Fleets' bonuses are now aggregated in their commission and the final sum is displayed only as one row: commission row. For example;

Commission: 100€, Bonuses 25€, Booking Fee 15€, Refunds 10€

Driver will only see a single row in their commission invoice in the amount of 50€ (100-25-15-10).

So, technically [actual commission - bounses/compensations - rider discounts - booking fees = commission on the invoice]

the report show the gross commission (the report shows the commission before all these discounts). on the invoice, the amount is all other things deducted from it (since commission netting is active).

More info about dynamic commission is [here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/3663265890].

{{art. 94º, nº 2, do Código de Processo Penal}}

1 - Os actos processuais que tiverem de praticar-se sob a forma escrita são redigidos de modo perfeitamente legível, não contendo espaços em branco que não sejam inutilizados, nem entrelinhas, rasuras ou emendas que não sejam ressalvadas.
       2 - Podem utilizar-se máquinas de escrever ou processadores de texto, caso em que se certifica, antes da assinatura, que o documento foi integralmente revisto e se identifica a entidade que o elaborou.
       3 - Podem igualmente utilizar-se fórmulas pré-impressas, formulários em suporte electrónico ou carimbos, a completar com o texto respectivo, podendo recorrer-se a assinatura electrónica certificada.
       4 - Em caso de manifesta ilegibilidade do documento, qualquer participante processual interessado pode solicitar, sem encargos, a respectiva transcrição dactilográfica.
       5 - As abreviaturas a que houver de recorrer-se devem possuir significado inequívoco. As datas e os números podem ser escritos por algarismos, ressalvada a indicação por extenso das penas, montantes indemnizatórios e outros elementos cuja certeza importe acautelar.
       6 - É obrigatória a menção do dia, mês e ano da prática do acto, bem como, tratando-se de acto que afecte liberdades fundamentais das pessoas, da hora da sua ocorrência, com referência ao momento do respectivo início e conclusão. O lugar da prática do acto deve ser indicado.

1 - Procedural acts that have to be carried out in written form shall be drafted in a perfectly legible manner, containing no blank spaces that are not erased, and no interlineations, erasures or amendments that are not highlighted.
       2 - Typewriters or word processors may be used, in which case it must be certified before signing that the document has been fully proofread and the organisation that drew it up must be identified.
       3 - Pre-printed formulae, electronic forms or stamps may also be used, to be completed with the respective text, and a certified electronic signature may be used.
       4 - If the document is clearly illegible, any interested procedural participant may request a typed transcription free of charge.
       5 - The abbreviations used must have an unambiguous meaning. Dates and numbers may be written in figures, with the exception of the indication in full of penalties, compensation amounts and other elements whose certainty must be safeguarded.
       6 - The day, month and year of the act must be mentioned, as well as, in the case of an act affecting people's fundamental freedoms, the time of its occurrence, with reference to the moment of its beginning and conclusion. The place where the act was carried out must be indicated.

{code:sql}with orders as (
select
	a.created						as comment_created
	, a.sender_type 
	, a.city_id
	, a.order_id
	, b.client_cancelled 
	, b.client_cancellation_reason 
	, b.driver_cancellation_reason 
	, b.is_positive 
	, b.negative_rules 
	, b.driver_id 
	, b.order_try_id 
	, b.created 					as order_created
	, row_number () over (partition by a.created order by b.created desc) 	as order_rw_nmbr
from comms.chat_profanity_detected 									as a
left join ng_public.driver_behavior_quality_driver_behavior_quality__order 	as b
	on a.order_id = b.order_id 
	and a.city_id = b.city_id 
	and a.created >= b.created
where 1=1
	and a.sender_type = 'rider'
	and a.order_system = 'taxi'
	and date(a.created_hour) >= date('2023-06-01')
	and date(a.created_hour) <= date('2023-07-31')
	and date(b.created_date) >= date('2023-06-01')
	and date(b.created_date) <= date('2023-07-31')
),
orders_edited as (
select 
	o.comment_created
	, o.sender_type
	, o.city_id
	, o.order_id
	, o.client_cancelled 
	, o.client_cancellation_reason 
	, o.driver_cancellation_reason 
	, o.is_positive 
	, o.negative_rules 
	, o.driver_id 
	, o.order_try_id
	, o.order_created
	, o.order_rw_nmbr
	, c.id 						as support_case_id
	, c.user_persona
	, c."source"
	, row_number () over (partition by o.order_try_id order by o.comment_created asc) as order_try_rw_nmbr
from orders 						 								as o
left join ng_customer_support.etl_data_api_support_case 					as c
	on o.order_id = c.order_id 
	and o.city_id = c.city_id 
	and o.driver_id = c.user_id 
	and c.user_persona = 'driver'
where 1=1
	and o.order_rw_nmbr = 1
	and date(c.created_date) >= date('2023-06-01')
	and c."source" <> 'beehive_outgoing'
)
select 
	oe.city_id
	, oe.order_id
	, oe.order_try_id
	, oe.client_cancelled
	, oe.client_cancellation_reason
	, case when oe.driver_cancellation_reason is not null then true
		else false end 				as driver_cancelled
	, oe.driver_cancellation_reason
	, oe.is_positive 					as driver_score_signal_is_positive
	, oe.negative_rules 				as negative_rules_triggered
	, oe.driver_id
	, case when oe.support_case_id is not null then true
		else false end 				as driver_raised_case
	, oe.support_case_id				as driver_case_id
	, oe."source" 						as driver_case_source
from orders_edited as oe
where 1=1
	and oe.order_try_rw_nmbr = 1

*Initial question:*

We would appreciate it if you clarify the below question to ensure that Bolt is compliant when arranging lottery campaigns for our drivers.

Bolt plans to launch a campaign in which drivers will be asked to complete specific numbers of rides (70/100/130) per week. If they complete a set number of trips, they will receive certain points. In the end, drivers could exchange these points for guaranteed prizes. Also, drivers who have completed at least 100 rides per week will participate in an additional lottery for a price.

# Please clarify whether it is mandatory to draft special terms and conditions for this campaign. If yes, should drivers, who want to participate, explicitly accept these terms? *OR*
# Is it sufficient to provide general information/overview about the campaign without specific Terms and Conditions and without asking explicit consent from every driver who wants to participate? It would be more efficient if we could send an email notification with campaign terms to all drivers instead of drafting specific terms. Please confirm if this is sufficient.

Since we plan to launch the campaign at the end of next week, we would highly appreciate your prompt reply at the beginning of next week.

*Answer of the Gaming Control Authority:*

Thank you for your request. Please find below our replay to Your questions.

We would like to inform You that lottery activities in Lithuania are being regulated by the Law on Lotteries of the Republic of Lithuania (hereinafter – Law on Lotteries).

Under the Law on Lotteries lottery is defined as a game with established rules where players buy tickets for a chance to win cash and (or) goods, and (or) gratuitous services. 

In accordance with the provisions of the Law on Lotteries, a game is considered to be a lottery if it meets +all+ the following criteria: 1) players buy tickets; 2) players participate in a game based on chance / success; 3) players risk to lose the amount paid for a ticket.

The description of the game in Your request shows that Bolt drivers, wishing to participate in the game, musn’t  receive a ticket for a set fee – they must complete specific numbers of rides per week and receive points. The game, described in Your e-mail, is not based on chance / success – drivers can exchange the points for guaranteed prizes. If drivers with 100 points will participate in additional lottery with the same conditions, under the Law on Lotteries the game described in Your request does not match the criteria of a lottery.

Gaming Control Authority under the Ministry of Finance of the Republic of Lithuania supervises only lottery operators and conditions of games which matches the criteria of a lottery. We would recommend to inform Bolt drivers about terms and conditions of the game in one of two ways that are described in Your request.
